title: Console core parcelization: scope cuts and minimal dashboard delivery plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: define a narrowly scoped, production-safe console surface that delivers immediate value for customers (cost per-route summary, latency vitals, and a lightweight trace sampler) while deferring high-cost telemetry features to later phases. This ticket captures the proposed MVP cuts, rationale, acceptance criteria, and rollout guardrails for the Console-Launch-2025 initiative. Background: telemetry budget and backend ingestion capacity forces a reduction of real-time tracing and detailed per-route breakdowns. We must preserve core user flows for incident triage and cost visibility while protecting SLOs and launch timeline.
problem_statement: Full feature set (per-request full traces, 30d raw span retention, per-route flamegraphs, and high-cardinality tag search) exceeds telemetry budget and implementation timeline. Without cuts we risk delaying launch by >=8 weeks or incurring significant infra costs.
proposed_scope_changes: Deliver a single consolidated 'Route Cost Summary' card per service instead of per-route deep-card set
Replace full-span real-time traces with a sampled trace viewer (1% default, adjustable per-customer tier) and a deterministic trace retrieval API for on-demand deep dives
Limit trace retention in the launch phase to 7 days for sampled traces; raw spans beyond that are archived to cold storage for enterprise customers only
Expose token-level cost breakdown as an aggregated daily bucketed metric (cost/dataset/route) rather than live per-request cost streaming
Defer: per-route flamegraphs, trace span search, and trace-based alerting to post-GA roadmap (Q2+)
Implement graceful 'degraded insights' UX states for routes with insufficient telemetry (explain sampling and retention to users)
Constrain trace ingestion rate with a server-side throttling policy tied to dedicated capacity and hosted tiers to protect SLOs
tradeoffs_and_rationale: Sampling reduces immediate triage fidelity but preserves launch schedule and keeps operational cost predictable
Aggregated cost buckets provide actionable economics without the expensive per-request instrumentation pipeline
Shorter retention reduces debugging window; mitigated by export to cold storage for enterprise customers and improved debugging playbooks in docs
Deferment of search and flamegraphs reduces backend complexity and buys time to mature trace indexing without harming core incident flows
acceptance_criteria: A1: Route Cost Summary card present on service overview showing 24h/7d cost delta and top-3 contributing routes
A2: Lightweight trace viewer available from an example failed request in the dashboard with sampling default=1% and a visible sampling badge
A3: Token-level cost exposed as daily aggregated metric in cost export (CSV/JSON) and shown in the cost breakdown card with clear unit labels
A4: Trace retention policy enforced: sampled traces retained 7 days in hot store; enterprise flag toggles 30d archival to cold store
A5: UX shows an explicit ‘degraded insights’ banner when sampling or retention limits omit data required for a view
A6: Backend throttling prevents trace ingestion from exceeding allocated capacity in staging tests (simulate 3x expected ingress and verify throttling kicks in)

decisions: D1: Default sampling rate = 1% on hosted tier; allow override per-customer via dedicated/private config (decision by Eng + PM 2025-02-20)
D2: Implement aggregated cost buckets (daily) for GA, postpone real-time per-request billing UI (decision 2025-02-15)
D3: Trace retention hot store = 7d for sampled traces; enterprise customers can opt into 30d cold archive (decision 2025-02-27)
D4: UX must surface sampling/retention limits in-context; no hidden data loss for users (decision 2025-02-26)
D5: Post-GA roadmap items (span search, flamegraph, trace alerting) to be scoped as separate PM epics (Q2/Q3)
D6: Security review required for trace export — notify Security and Compliance (decision 2025-03-01)
